Through EnergizeDB®, TechResources™, TechStudio™, TechTalks™, TechEvents™, and TechChannels™, we help B2B technology brands reach relevant decision-makers, establish authority, activate demand, and create stronger paths to qualified pipeline.

Understand why the result occurred and what it tells us about the audience. 7. Scale what works. Increase investment, transfer the learning or develop the next test. description: Quadrangle is a customer strategy consultancy, not a research agency that hands over a report and moves on. For nearly 40 years, it has combined a research skillset with a consultancy mindset, turning what customers value into decisions a board can act on. Our belief is simple. Customers create the value in brands. Price, product and process only matter in relation to what a customer perceives them to be worth, and that perception is where commercial advantage is won or lost. Every engagement sits inside one of three areas. Strategic insight turns customer evidence into commercial direction: a specific answer on what to do next, and why it will pay off. Compelling propositions close the gap between what a brand assumes customers want and what they actually value, then design around the difference. Distinctive positioning helps a brand choose what to be, and what not to be, in a market where too many competitors sound the same. Quadrangle works with senior decision-makers, typically Commercial Directors, Heads of Brand and CMOs, in financial services, travel and transport, and retail. These are markets where the product is often functionally similar across providers, and where the real contest for customer choice happens elsewhere: in perception, relationship and trust. Most clients have been through the alternative. Agencies that arrive, produce a deck, and disappear before the recommendation is tested against a real decision. Quadrangle's model is built differently: senior people stay on the account from the brief to the boardroom, not just for the pitch. Price is one input into that perception, and rarely the deciding one. Quadrangle's own framework for it, the 7 Sources of Customer Value, sets out seven distinct dimensions that decide whether customers see a brand as essential or interchangeable: utility, quality, value for money, ease, experience, brand fit and engagement. Value for money sits inside that list as one source among seven, not the whole story. Two suppliers can be priced identically and perceived completely differently, because the other six sources are doing the rest of the work: trust, ease of doing business, and the strength of the relationship. That is why some suppliers become difficult to replace even when a cheaper alternative exists on paper. It is also the argument Quadrangle makes about its own market. The firm competes in a category where senior buyers could, in theory, choose on day rate alone. Almost none of them do. For marketers in the room at B2B Marketing Live, the same principle runs inward as well as outward. Every supplier decision your business makes, and every one your customers make about you, runs on the same psychology: brand, trust and perceived value, not price in isolation. Quadrangle's session, "If It Was Just About Price, We'd All Buy the Cheapest," sets out the seven sources of value that decide whether a business gets chosen, retained or replaced, in your own supplier relationships and in the brand you are building for your customers. To talk to Quadrangle about a supplier, brand or proposition problem your business is wrestling with, find us in the Discovery Zone.
